description: Single-panel line plot (no sub-images) comparing measured and simulated yield strength of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel as a function of multiaxial forging (MAF) pass number. The y-axis is labelled "Yield strength (MPa)" and spans 200 to 1600 with gridline ticks every 200 MPa; the x-axis is labelled "No. of Pass" with integer ticks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The legend identifies a solid line with square markers as "Experimental" and a dashed line with circular markers as "FE simulation". Both curves rise steeply from a common value just below the 400 MPa gridline at 0 pass; after one pass the Experimental point sits just above the 1000 MPa gridline and the FE simulation point just below it. Between 1 and 3 passes the two curves nearly converge between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines. At 5 passes the Experimental point lies between the 1400 and 1600 MPa gridlines (closer to 1600) while the FE simulation point lies only slightly above 1400 MPa, i.e. the simulation underestimates the measured value most strongly at the highest pass number. No numerical data labels are printed. The figure demonstrates that the modified J-C / FEA prediction tracks the experimental strengthening closely around 3 passes but deviates at 1 and at 5 passes.

subfigures.description: Line plot of yield strength vs number of MAF passes, y-axis 'Yield strength (MPa)' (200-1600, step 200), x-axis 'No. of Pass' (0-5). Two series: solid line with square markers labelled 'Experimental' and dashed line with circular markers labelled 'FE simulation'. Both rise steeply from 0 to 1 pass; the Experimental curve lies above the FE curve at 1 and 5 passes and the two nearly coincide at 3 passes. No numeric data labels are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line plot with y-axis labelled "Yield strength (MPa)" (ticks 200-1600, step 200) and x-axis labelled "No. of Pass" (integer ticks 0-5).
The legend gives two series: a solid line with square markers labelled "Experimental" and a dashed line with circular markers labelled "FE simulation".
At 0 pass the Experimental and FE simulation markers practically coincide, both lying just below the 400 MPa gridline.
The steepest rise of both curves occurs between 0 and 1 pass.
At 1 pass the Experimental point lies just above the 1000 MPa gridline whereas the FE simulation point lies just below it, the largest visible separation between the two series.
At 3 passes the Experimental and FE simulation curves nearly coincide between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines.

At 5 passes the Experimental point lies between the 1400 and 1600 MPa gridlines (closer to 1600) while the FE simulation point lies only slightly above the 1400 MPa gridline, so the simulation under-predicts the measured yield strength.
No numerical data labels, error bars or fit statistics are printed on the plot; values can only be read against the 200 MPa gridlines.
The caption states the figure is "Prediction of yield strength with respect to experimental results." and gives no numeric values.
The citing text states that Fig. 13 shows the comparison of experimental yield strength values with the simulated yield strengths.

The citing text states that up to 3 passes the finite element simulation predicts strengthening similar to the measured yield value, while after three passes the predicted value "shows a lower deviation from the experimental results"; the wording is ambiguous, and the plotted points instead show a visible gap again at 5 passes, so caption text and pixels do not fully agree (both readings reported).

The citing text states the material is Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel processed by multiaxial forging with 33% normal strain per pass, and the modified J-C model (Eq. 6) incorporates strain-dependent dislocation density (Eq. 7) and grain size (Eq. 8) measured by XRD (Fig. 5) and EBSD (Fig. 8).
The plotted pass numbers correspond to MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 stages referred to in the citing text, plus the 0-pass starting condition.
